title: Throwing and Aiming Games
strapline: Beanbags, buckets and a good aim — power, control and a bit of maths.
intent: Throwing, rolling and aiming develop hand-eye coordination and gross-motor control.
Adjusting how hard and where to throw is real problem-solving through the body.
Keeping a simple score brings counting and comparing into play with a purpose.
Taking turns and cheering for others builds patience and social warmth.
Getting a little better each go grows persistence and self-belief.
implementation: Offer beanbags, soft balls and quoits with a range of targets at different distances.
Include throwing, rolling and dropping-in targets so different skills get a go.
Model an over-arm and an under-arm throw, then let children find what works.
Move targets nearer or further to keep every child on the edge of success.
Count hits together and compare — "you got three, how many did you get?".
Keep it cooperative as often as competitive — "how many can we get as a team?".
key_questions: How hard will you need to throw to reach that one?
Which target is easiest — and which is the real challenge?
How many did you get in? How could we count them?
What happens if you aim a bit higher?
Shall we try together and add up our score?

impact.text: Children throw, roll and aim with increasing control and coordination.
Children adjust their throw after a miss, working out how to succeed.
Children count their hits and compare amounts in a real context.
Children take turns and celebrate each other's successes.
Children keep going after a miss and take pride in improving.

enhancements: Beanbags, quoits and soft balls in different sizes and weights.
Buckets, hoops and chalked targets at varying distances.
A number line or scoreboard for counting hits.
A "near / far" set of targets so difficulty can be chosen.
A team target for cooperative counting.
Chalk to mark a throwing line and redraw targets.

playing_exploring: Children experiment with force and aim, finding out what works.
active_learning: Children keep trying after a miss and take satisfaction in improving.
creating_thinking: Children work out how to change their throw to hit a harder target.
